decisions.decision: Serve scores through a dedicated online inference service
decisions.context: Every card transaction needs a fraud score before authorization, with results in tens of milliseconds. The service must sustain peaks.

alternatives.label: Dedicated online inference service
pros: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: keep models loaded in memory
Peak availability: scale serving capacity independently
cons: Peak availability: adds a service dependency

alternatives.label: Run inference inside the authorization service
pros: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: avoids a network hop
cons: Peak availability: scoring competes with authorization workloads
Auditor traceability: model changes couple to service releases

alternatives.label: Call a hosted third-party scoring API
pros: Peak availability: provider manages serving capacity
cons: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: network and provider latency
Auditor traceability: less control over scoring records

decisions.rationale: Tens-of-milliseconds latency decides the choice: a dedicated service can keep models loaded and scale for scoring demand. It costs an additional service dependency.
consequences: Maintain a low-latency network path from authorization to scoring.
Scale serving capacity independently and monitor its availability.
Keep authorization behavior defined for scoring timeouts.

decisions.decision: Scale serving capacity for transaction peaks
decisions.context: Scoring must keep working during peaks, while each result must still arrive within tens of milliseconds. The brief does not specify peak size or request limits.

alternatives.label: Autoscale stateless inference replicas
pros: Peak availability: add replicas as demand rises
Tens-of-milliseconds latency: distribute requests across replicas
cons: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: scale-up delay can expose capacity gaps

alternatives.label: Maintain fixed excess capacity
pros: Peak availability: capacity is ready at peak onset
cons: Peak availability: excess capacity remains idle off-peak

alternatives.label: Queue requests when capacity is full
cons: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: queueing can exceed the scoring budget

decisions.rationale: Peak availability decides the choice: stateless replicas can add scoring capacity as demand rises. This gives up immediate protection from scale-up delay, which must be managed with capacity headroom.
consequences: Keep inference replicas stateless so they can scale horizontally.
Maintain headroom to cover demand while replicas start.
Set capacity limits and a policy for requests that exceed them.

decisions.decision: Record the model version and features for each score
decisions.context: Auditors must later be able to determine which model version and which features produced every score. That requires a durable association between each score and its scoring inputs.

alternatives.label: Persist score, model version, and feature snapshot asynchronously
pros: Auditor traceability: retains inputs and model identity per score
Tens-of-milliseconds latency: keeps durable writes off the response path
cons: Auditor traceability: asynchronous failure can leave gaps

alternatives.label: Persist score, model version, and feature snapshot synchronously
pros: Auditor traceability: confirms record persistence before replying
cons: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: storage writes add response time
Peak availability: storage outages can block scoring

alternatives.label: Persist score and model version only
pros: Tens-of-milliseconds latency: smaller records to write
cons: Auditor traceability: cannot reconstruct which features produced the score

chosen.label: Persist score, model version, and feature snapshot asynchronously

decisions.rationale: Auditor traceability decides the choice: retaining both the model version and feature snapshot supports later inspection. Asynchronous writes protect latency, at the cost of needing to detect and handle missing records.
consequences: Include a stable score identifier with each audit record.
Monitor delivery failures and record completeness.
Define retention and access controls for stored feature snapshots.

decisions.context: Auditors need the model version used for each score, so model identity must be explicit across deployments. The brief does not specify a release strategy.

alternatives.label: Versioned model artifacts with staged rollout and rollback
pros: Auditor traceability: immutable versions identify scoring behavior
Peak availability: rollback restores a known serving version
cons: Peak availability: staged rollout adds operational steps

alternatives.label: Replace the active model in place
cons: Auditor traceability: model identity can be ambiguous
Peak availability: rollback may require rebuilding the prior state

alternatives.label: Run a fixed model until a service release
pros: Peak availability: model and service change together
cons: Auditor traceability: version history needs release-level tracking
Peak availability: model updates depend on service rollout

chosen.label: Versioned model artifacts with staged rollout and rollback

decisions.rationale: Auditor traceability decides the choice: immutable model versions make each score’s model identity clear. Staged rollout adds release work, and the scoring path must handle version transitions safely.
consequences: Attach an immutable model version to every score record.
Retain prior artifacts for rollback and audit needs.
Coordinate staged rollout with serving capacity.

uncovered: Model training, validation, and promotion criteria.
Audit record retention period, storage system, and access policy.
Timeout, fallback, and authorization behavior when scoring is unavailable.
Peak volume, service-level target, and capacity limits.
